headline: US downgrades travel advisory for Bangladesh to Level 2
summary: The US government has shifted the advisory from Level 3 (Reconsider Travel) to Level 2 (Exercise Increased Caution), signaling increased confidence in the country's security.
details: The US has updated its travel advisory for Bangladesh, shifting it from Level 3 to Level 2, according to a statement from the foreign ministry.
The overall advisory has been lowered from 'Reconsider Travel' to 'Exercise Increased Caution', reflecting that Bangladesh is now considered safer for travel.
This development follows a bilateral meeting in Dhaka on Thursday between Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman and US Special Envoy Sergio Gor.
US Special Envoy Sergio Gor informed Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman of the update via a text message immediately after their meeting.
The foreign ministry stated that the improvement reflects growing US confidence in Bangladesh's overall security environment and stability.
The Bangladesh government views this as recognition of its efforts to ensure security, stability, and a better environment for international travel, trade, and investment.

headline_marked: Bangladesh Bank [[cuts policy rate to 9.50%]] to boost investment
headline: Bangladesh Bank cuts policy rate to 9.50% to boost investment
summary: The central bank reduced the repo rate by 50 basis points after 21 months to encourage business growth and create more jobs.
details: Bangladesh Bank has reduced its policy rate, known as the repo rate, from 10% to 9.50% in an effort to lower loan interest rates for borrowers and stimulate investment and employment.
The decision was made during the 13th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), chaired by Governor Mostakur Rahman. The new rate will take effect from August 2.
The central bank stated that the cut was based on a review of domestic and global inflation, private sector credit flow, economic growth, and the balance of payments.
The move comes as private investment as a percentage of GDP reached its lowest point in 14 years in the last fiscal year, amid political uncertainty and economic crises.
Additionally, the latest labor force survey shows a rise in unemployment among educated youth, with one in three graduates currently unemployed, totaling approximately 9 lakh people.
To combat high inflation, the central bank had previously raised the policy rate in 11 consecutive stages up to 10% by October 2024.
While inflation remains high, above 9%, the central bank believes that encouraging new investment will help accelerate overall economic growth and create necessary jobs.
Alongside the policy rate, the Standing Lending Facility (SLF) rate has been reduced from 11.50% to 11%, while the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate remains unchanged at 7.50%.

Bangladesh Bank cuts policy rate to 9.50% after 21 months to revive investment and tackle unemployment.

Bangladesh Bank has reduced its policy rate, known as the repo rate, from 10% to 9.50% in an effort to lower loan interest rates for borrowers and stimulate investment and employment.

The decision was made during the 13th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), chaired by Governor Mostakur Rahman. The new rate will take effect from August 2.

The central bank stated that the cut was based on a review of domestic and global inflation, private sector credit flow, economic growth, and the balance of payments.

The move comes as private investment as a percentage of GDP reached its lowest point in 14 years in the last fiscal year, amid political uncertainty and economic crises.

Additionally, the latest labor force survey shows a rise in unemployment among educated youth, with one in three graduates currently unemployed, totaling approximately 9 lakh people.

To combat high inflation, the central bank had previously raised the policy rate in 11 consecutive stages up to 10% by October 2024.

While inflation remains high, above 9%, the central bank believes that encouraging new investment will help accelerate overall economic growth and create necessary jobs.

Alongside the policy rate, the Standing Lending Facility (SLF) rate has been reduced from 11.50% to 11%, while the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate remains unchanged at 7.50%.
